title: Duchy of Florence
capsule: The Duchy of Florence was established in 1532 when Pope Clement VII (Giulio de' Medici) imposed Alessandro de' Medici as hereditary duke over the former Florentine Republic, which had just been crushed by Habsburg and papal forces. Alessandro's brief tyrannical rule ended with his assassination in January 1537 by his cousin Lorenzino de' Medici. The Senate of Florence then chose Cosimo I de' Medici, eighteen years old, as the new duke; Cosimo swiftly defeated the republican exiles at the Battle of Montemurlo (August 1537), consolidated his grip on the Florentine state, and expanded its territory by acquiring Siena in 1555. In 1569 Pope Pius V elevated Cosimo to Grand Duke of Tuscany, transforming the duchy into a regional power.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The duchy's territory is well documented through Florentine administrative and cartographic sources; the 1532–1569 period's boundaries are clearly defined, though control over some smaller subject communes varied.
